active_paradigms.idea: Replace prefix-only bounded DFS with an exact transposition-table search keyed by selected-set plus simulator-relevant frontier signature
active_paradigms.description: The current program first uses a width-8 beam, then insertion descent, and finally a prefix DFS that evaluates at most 120k/300k nodes. Its main strength is that every ordering decision is scored with the real simulator objective rather than an operation-count proxy. Its principal weakness is that `cost(prefix)` caches almost no equivalent work: two different prefixes with the same completed transactions are treated as unrelated, even when they induce the same remaining conflict frontier. Build a state signature from the actual parsed transactions: selected transaction bitmask, and for every key touched by an unfinished transaction, the identity/order-position of the most recent selected writer plus the set of selected readers since that writer when such reads affect future dependencies. Memoize the best achievable prefix makespan or nondominated simulator frontier per signature, and prune a newly reached signature when its current simulator cost is no better than the recorded one. This is a state-space shortest-path/dynamic-programming formulation rather than the current factorial tree over literal prefixes. Expand candidates in increasing real child cost, preserving the existing beam result as an incumbent, but do not rely on the potentially fragile regex-based generic `__dict__` discovery: parse the workload representation used by `Workload` explicitly. This can prove or search much more deeply than the present node cap because many different interleavings collapse into one dependency-equivalent state.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary scalar score: simulator makespan returned by `workload.get_opt_seq_cost`; specifically reduce missed improvements caused by the current shallow prefix DFS and prefix-only cache.
active_paradigms.cautions: The signature must retain every fact that can change dependencies of future operations; a selected-set mask alone is not valid because conflict directions depend on order. If the simulator semantics cannot be reconstructed exactly, use the signature only for safe dominance checks confirmed by equal simulator frontier metadata, never as an assumed equivalence. Do not retain the current rule that marks transactions conflicting whenever transaction text cannot be recovered, since that silently eliminates valid commutations and weakens search.

active_paradigms.idea: Use deterministic exhaustive large-neighborhood optimization around conflict-dense transaction blocks
active_paradigms.description: The current solution has useful real-cost beam seeding and one-transaction insertion descent, but a single insertion cannot cross the energy barriers created when several transactions must move together to change multiple conflict directions. Construct a schedule seed using the current beam result, identify a contiguous block around the transactions contributing to the latest completion path, and exhaustively evaluate every ordering of a small block such as 6 to 8 transactions while retaining all outside transactions fixed. Select the best real simulator-cost permutation of that block, then repeat only when an improvement occurs; expand the block around newly critical transactions rather than using random restarts. This is materially different from global factorial enumeration, which previously failed, because its cost is bounded by `k!` and it searches the coupled moves that insertion descent cannot express. Use overlapping windows and windows formed from conflict-neighborhood positions, not merely index-adjacent windows, so transactions that share hot keys can be optimized jointly even if the seed placed them apart. Preserve deterministic tie-breaking by transaction ID, which improves evaluator consistency. Because the evaluator wrapper exposes no additional secondary metric, all acceptance decisions should use the exact returned makespan, never an estimated conflict count.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary makespan, by changing several mutually interacting transaction precedences in one exact move and escaping local optima of insertion-only descent.
active_paradigms.cautions: This should be bounded tightly: 8! evaluations can already be expensive when `get_opt_seq_cost` is costly, so adapt the block size to transaction count and elapsed time. Recompute candidates from the original schedule for each window; incremental mutation errors easily produce duplicates or missing transaction IDs. The prior failed `itertools.permutations` idea was full permutation enumeration, whereas this must remain a targeted bounded neighborhood based on simulator-critical conflicts.

active_paradigms.idea: Apply a dominance-aware Pareto frontier search over partial schedules using actual prefix makespan and remaining-conflict pressure
active_paradigms.description: The existing beam keeps only the eight partial schedules with smallest current prefix cost. This is myopic: a slightly more expensive prefix can orient hot-key conflicts favorably and produce a much lower final makespan, while the current beam discards it before DFS reaches it. Maintain a bounded nondominated frontier of prefixes at every depth, with objective one equal to exact `get_opt_seq_cost(prefix)` and objective two a lower-bound estimate of unavoidable remaining work, such as the maximum per-transaction operation tail and per-key write/read conflict-chain tail implied by the prefix. Use `bisect.insort` to maintain the frontier sorted by the lexicographic pair and discard a prefix only if another prefix has no greater exact prefix cost and no greater admissible remaining lower bound. Candidate generation remains based on actual simulator child costs, but retain diverse conflict orientations rather than only the cheapest eight prefixes. At completion, evaluate every retained full order exactly and use it as the incumbent for the exact/dominance search. This directly addresses the current program’s strongest limitation—hard width-8 truncation—without using random shuffles, heap best-first search, MILP, or a continuous surrogate. It also gives a principled way to allocate the fixed search budget toward prefixes that can still beat the incumbent.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary makespan and robustness across all evaluator workloads; retain schedules with a temporarily worse prefix cost but substantially less unavoidable future serialization.
active_paradigms.cautions: The second quantity must be an admissible lower bound if it is used for correctness pruning; if it is only a heuristic, use it solely to rank or diversify the bounded frontier. Do not claim that the sum of per-key tails is a lower bound, because different keys can execute in parallel; use maxima or a proven critical-chain bound. Keep exact schedule tuples with each frontier entry because two prefixes with equal scalar scores may have different future conflict orientations.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use randomized iterated local search with shuffle-based diverse restarts and full swap/block neighborhoods
tried_paradigms.description: The current code starts from a single narrow-beam solution and accepts only strictly improving one-transaction relocations, so it stops at the first insertion-local optimum. Use `random.shuffle` to generate diverse transaction permutations or diverse tie orders, refine each with simulator-evaluated local search, and retain the best complete schedule across `num_seqs` restarts. Within a restart, evaluate both pairwise swaps and remove-and-reinsert moves; swaps are important because a beneficial exchange can require moving both transactions, while the current first-improvement relocation may require a temporary worsening move and cannot cross that barrier. Use best-improvement selection per local-search pass rather than committing to the first detected improvement, then repeat until neither neighborhood improves. Seed some restarts from the beam solution after a substantial random perturbation, and seed others from completely shuffled schedules, so the search explores both nearby and distant basins. Every acceptance decision must use `workload.get_opt_seq_cost` on the complete candidate, not proxy statistics such as transaction length or write count. This turns `num_seqs` into actual diversification budget and is robust when a full branch-and-bound search is too expensive.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Best complete-schedule makespan over multiple independent local-optimum basins; this specifically targets improvements unavailable to strict single-start insertion descent.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Cache evaluated complete permutation tuples during a restart or globally to avoid repeatedly invoking the simulator for the same swap/insertion result. Keep randomization reproducible with a fixed seed unless the benchmark intentionally rewards stochastic variation. Full swap plus all insertion evaluations cost O(n^3) simulator calls per pass, so cap passes or use candidate lists for very large n; never replace final candidate evaluation with a heuristic estimate.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use exact permutation enumeration for small transaction sets via itertools.permutations
tried_paradigms.description: The current program performs a width-8 beam search using the simulator cost of an incomplete prefix, then applies only three rounds of one-transaction relocation. Its strength is that every retained candidate and every local-search move is evaluated by workload.get_opt_seq_cost, so it optimizes the actual hidden conflict/makespan semantics rather than a proxy. Its major weakness is beam pruning: a prefix with a slightly worse partial cost may enable a much better final interleaving, but is irreversibly discarded before local search begins. Add an exact mode when workload.num_txns is small enough that n! simulator evaluations fit the evaluation budget, for example n <= 9 or a dynamically chosen factorial budget. Enumerate each complete permutation, evaluate workload.get_opt_seq_cost on that complete sequence, and return the best schedule directly. This is fundamentally stronger than any prefix beam because it never assumes that prefix makespan ranks final makespan correctly. Keep the current heuristic only as the fallback for larger n, since the evaluator accepts a schedule and scores it through the actual simulator.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Direct minimization of the hidden evaluator's primary makespan for small workloads; this removes beam-pruning error completely and is deterministic.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The visible evaluator is only a lock-wrapped forwarding function, so no secondary metric or score aggregation is exposed; do not optimize an invented surrogate. Put a strict cap on the number of complete schedules evaluated, since factorial growth is severe. Tie-break equal costs deterministically to avoid run-to-run differences.

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve a direct precedence-and-makespan mixed-integer model with scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: Replace prefix-cost ranking with a single global discrete optimization model whenever the conflict relation can be reconstructed from the transaction operation strings. Create binary precedence variables x[i,j] indicating whether transaction i is before transaction j, impose x[i,j] + x[j,i] = 1, and add triangle/transitivity constraints or an equivalent integer rank variable for each transaction. Build operation start-time variables and a makespan variable C; preserve every operation's within-transaction order and add disjunctive precedence constraints for every cross-transaction read/write or write/write conflict on the same key, gated by the corresponding transaction-order binary. Minimize C with scipy.optimize.milp and then sort transactions by the solved rank variables to produce the required sequence. This directly targets global makespan instead of the current beam's incomplete-prefix cost, and it can retain globally useful choices that local relocation cannot reach. Validate the extracted order once with workload.get_opt_seq_cost; if the simulator’s exact locking semantics differ from the reconstructed constraints, use the solver result as a high-quality initial schedule for the existing exact-cost improvement logic rather than trusting the model’s objective alone. The model is especially promising when conflicts are sparse, because only conflicting operation pairs need constraints.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The actual makespan lower-level precedence structure globally, rather than a heuristic ordering score; potentially proves optimality or provides a strong global lower bound.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This is valid only if Workload exposes or permits parsing transaction operations and its simulator semantics can be modeled faithfully. Big-M constants must be safe but reasonably tight, operation durations must match the simulator, and all conflicting read/write pairs—not read/read pairs—must be represented. Dense workloads can create too many binary variables and constraints, so gate this mode by transaction/operation count and use a solver time limit.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use NetworkX minimum-fill tree decomposition to exploit sparse conflict graph separators
tried_paradigms.description: Construct the undirected transaction conflict graph, with an edge exactly when two transactions access a common key and at least one access is a write. The present beam method treats every remaining transaction as globally coupled, although independent connected components and small graph separators create substantial exact structure. Call networkx.algorithms.approximation.treewidth_min_fill_in to obtain a low-width elimination/decomposition guide for this graph. Use the resulting bags to perform exact dynamic programming over boundary transaction orders: retain only the relative order and simulator-relevant frontier state for transactions crossing a separator, while optimize transactions internal to a bag before forgetting them. At a minimum, disconnected components should be optimized separately and then merged by testing component-level interleavings with actual get_opt_seq_cost; a true decomposition DP extends this benefit to nearly separable sparse graphs. Each completed candidate must still be scored by workload.get_opt_seq_cost, preserving alignment with the hidden evaluator despite the evaluator source itself not being visible beyond the wrapper. This attacks a different weakness from wider beam search: it reduces combinatorial dimension according to actual conflict topology instead of arbitrary beam width.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Makespan on sparse or modular workloads by avoiding needless global permutation search and preserving exact alternatives across small conflict separators.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The minimum-fill decomposition is heuristic and only valuable when the conflict graph has low effective treewidth; dense all-to-all conflict workloads should fall back to direct search. A graph edge must reflect the simulator’s precise conflict definition, including write-write and read-write but excluding read-read. Do not assume independently optimized components can simply be concatenated: test merges with the actual cost oracle because nonconflicting transactions may beneficially overlap.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use exact branch-and-bound with conflict-commutation canonicalization, memoized by functools.lru_cache
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is a width-8 prefix beam search: it evaluates every one-transaction extension with the real simulator, retains only eight low-cost prefixes, then reaches a 1-move insertion local optimum. This is strong because it optimizes the actual makespan rather than a length/write-count proxy, but its prefix truncation can permanently discard an order whose early prefix is expensive but whose later conflict overlap is excellent. Replace beam truncation for tractable instances with depth-first branch-and-bound over complete transaction permutations. Treat the current beam-plus-insertion result as the initial incumbent, so pruning begins with a strong upper bound. A partial sequence's simulator makespan is a valid monotone lower bound if adding transactions cannot shorten an already scheduled prefix; prune whenever that lower bound is at least the incumbent. Before branching, identify pairs of remaining transactions that have no read/write conflict on any item and impose a deterministic canonical order on such interchangeable choices, avoiding exploration of equivalent permutations. Use functools.lru_cache for conflict-pair tests and for each evaluated prefix tuple's exact simulator cost. Retain the current beam method only as a time-bounded fallback when the exact search node budget is exceeded.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimizes the sole evaluated quantity, the real workload.get_opt_seq_cost makespan, while eliminating the beam's irreversible early-prefix mistakes.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not cache only by the set of selected transactions: different orders of the same set can produce different simulator states and costs. Commutation pruning is safe only when two transactions have no shared key for which at least one access is a write; read/read overlap is nonconflicting. Keep a strict node/time budget and always return the incumbent schedule, because exhaustive search remains factorial on dense large workloads.

tried_paradigms.idea: Apply deterministic very-large-neighborhood descent by exhaustively permuting a contiguous transaction window with itertools.permutations
tried_paradigms.description: The present insertion phase is already a complete 1-transaction relocation neighborhood, repeated three times, so merely adding swaps or more random restarts is unlikely to escape its local minima; randomized iterated local search was also already unsuccessful. Use a different neighborhood: select a contiguous window of k transactions in the incumbent order, keep all transactions outside the window fixed, and enumerate every ordering of the k removed transactions with itertools.permutations. Score each reconstructed full sequence using workload.get_opt_seq_cost and accept the best strict improvement for that window. A window of 5 has only 120 candidates and a window of 6 has 720, yet it can reverse several mutually conflicting transactions simultaneously, which a monotone insertion descent often cannot do. Sweep windows around high-conflict boundaries first, where adjacent transactions share write-related keys, rather than spending calls on unrelated regions. Continue until one full deterministic sweep produces no improving window; optionally alternate k=5 and k=6 if the evaluation budget permits. This is an exact optimizer over each selected neighborhood and always preserves or improves the current real score.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape 1-move insertion local minima caused by coupled conflict chains, using only exact full-schedule makespan evaluations.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not compare partial-window costs: each candidate must be evaluated as the complete order because downstream operation overlap determines the score. Deduplicate candidates when a window contains transactions with identical conflict signatures, and use strict '<' acceptance to avoid cycles and score-noise churn. Cap k conservatively: k=7 already requires 5,040 simulator calls per window.

tried_paradigms.idea: Generate a conflict-locality schedule with scipy.sparse.csgraph.reverse_cuthill_mckee as a deterministic independent seed
tried_paradigms.description: Current beam construction has very little diversity: all survivors are chosen solely by short-prefix cost, so they commonly collapse into the same region before insertion begins. Construct a sparse undirected transaction conflict matrix whose edge weight is the number of shared keys with at least one write, optionally multiplied by the number of conflicting operation pairs. Call scipy.sparse.csgraph.reverse_cuthill_mckee on this matrix to obtain a transaction order that minimizes the bandwidth of the conflict graph; evaluate both that order and its reversal with the real simulator and retain the better one as an alternative candidate. The structural rationale is that transactions which strongly conflict are brought close in the serial order, reducing long-range chains in which a transaction's late write stalls many otherwise independent operations. This is fundamentally unlike random restart, failed connected-component decomposition, and prefix beam scoring: it uses the global conflict topology in one deterministic graph ordering call. Compare this complete structural schedule directly against the beam-and-insertion output, returning whichever has lower get_opt_seq_cost. If desired, use the graph order as the incumbent for the exact or window optimizer rather than running an additional unrelated heuristic pipeline.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Provides a globally diverse, conflict-aware full permutation that can beat a beam trapped by misleading prefix makespans, while final selection remains based solely on actual makespan.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The matrix must include only read/write and write/write relationships; read/read sharing must contribute zero. Reverse Cuthill-McKee operates on a sparse symmetric graph and does not itself know operation timing, so never return it without evaluating its actual simulator cost. Isolated transactions may be ordered arbitrarily and should not be interpreted as dependencies.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the unsafe independent-ID pruning with sound sleep-set partial-order reduction
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first constructs a width-8 simulator-scored beam, performs insertion descent, and then runs a prefix branch-and-bound search. Its useful properties are that every candidate is evaluated by the real simulator and prefix makespan is used as an admissible monotone lower bound. However, its rule that forbids choosing transaction j whenever a smaller currently remaining nonconflicting transaction i exists is not a valid symmetry rule. Although i and j commute with each other, either can conflict with a third transaction k, so forcing i before j can remove schedules such as j,k,i that are not equivalent to i,k,j. Replace this rule with a sleep-set scheme: at each search node retain transactions already explored by earlier siblings that commute with the chosen prefix extension, and suppress only choices proven redundant by adjacent commutations. When branching on transaction t, pass a child sleep set containing only previously slept transactions independent of t, then add earlier sibling choices that are independent of t to the sleep set for later siblings. Cache search states including the selected-set representation and sleep-set information only when the state semantics make them equivalent. This retains completeness over distinct conflict traces while still eliminating genuinely duplicate orders, allowing the incumbent to improve instead of accidentally proving over a restricted search space.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The actual simulator makespan, especially schedules currently excluded by invalid canonicalization; preserve valid pruning so the 18-second budget examines more useful prefixes.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not cache a result solely by the selected transaction set: the simulator cost and future precedence structure depend on the order of the prefix. Do not infer independence from transaction IDs or from read-read sharing alone unless transaction text has been parsed reliably. A sleep-set implementation must be tested on three-transaction patterns where two transactions are independent but both conflict with a third.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use exact critical-window reinsertion rather than one-transaction insertion descent
tried_paradigms.description: The current local improvement is only a 1-transaction insertion neighborhood, so it cannot cross a makespan barrier requiring two or more transactions to move together. After obtaining a schedule, identify the critical portion using repeated simulator evaluations: temporarily remove each transaction or contiguous interval and measure which removals reduce the makespan most. Select a small deterministic window of 3 to 6 transactions from that high-impact region, keep all other transactions in their relative order, and enumerate every combination of insertion positions of the removed transactions among the fixed backbone. For each position pattern, evaluate the actual completed order through get_opt_seq_cost and retain the best schedule, repeating only while it strictly improves. This is qualitatively different from random shuffle restarts and from failed full itertools.permutations enumeration: the factorial search is confined to a tiny causally relevant subset while positions in the rest of the sequence are considered exactly. It can repair coupled conflict directions, for example moving two writers ahead of a reader chain together, which no single insertion improves in isolation. Start with windows around transactions whose deletion has the highest measured cost reduction, rather than using lengths, write counts, or graph-only proxies.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escaping local optima of the existing beam plus single-insertion descent and directly lowering full-schedule simulator makespan.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Keep the removed set small enough that the product of internal orders and insertion-position choices fits the evaluation deadline. Deduplicate candidate tuples before simulator calls and use strict improvement to prevent cycles. This should be deterministic; randomized iterated local search was already unsuccessful and is not a substitute for exhaustive optimization of a selected critical window.

tried_paradigms.idea: Construct beam candidates using a critical-path-aware rollout score instead of raw prefix makespan
tried_paradigms.description: The existing beam ranks every partial order solely by get_opt_seq_cost(prefix). This is a weak discriminator early in the sequence: many prefixes have the same low current makespan even though one commits to a long future conflict chain. For each possible next transaction, evaluate the real prefix cost, then compute a deterministic rollout lower-bound surrogate from the unplaced transactions: aggregate, per data item, the remaining work involving that item and identify transactions that bridge multiple heavily contended items. Rank candidates lexicographically by current simulator prefix cost, estimated final critical load, and a stable transaction-ID tie breaker. The estimate must not replace the simulator objective; it should only decide which candidates enter the fixed-width beam and in what order DFS children are visited. A practical formulation is to build remaining per-key reader/writer incidence and score a transaction by the amount of future conflicting work it unlocks versus the maximum contention it leaves behind. Use numpy.argsort on a structured tuple/array of these candidate scores so all ties are stable and deterministic. This targets the principal weakness of a narrow width-8 beam: loss of diverse prefixes before the exact bounded search begins, while avoiding the previously failed heap-based best-first expansion and avoiding static transaction-length heuristics.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Quality of the initial incumbent and DFS branch ordering, which increases the amount of safe prefix pruning possible under the fixed node/time budget and therefore reduces simulator makespan.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The rollout estimate is not an admissible pruning bound, so never discard a DFS node based on it; use it only for ordering or beam selection. Parse operation sequences robustly and combine multiple accesses to the same key so a transaction is considered a writer if any of its accesses write. Preserve the raw simulator prefix cost as the first ranking key, since the evaluator scores only get_opt_seq_cost of the final returned order.
